attempts.summary: Deployed PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1/node2/node3 (CentOS Stream 10). Configured node1 as initial primary with node2 and node3 as async standbys via pg_basebackup, replication over scram-sha-256 auth with a role generated on-node and injected only via secret_env. Demonstrated failover: stopped node1 (simulated primary loss), promoted node2 with pg_promote(), verified zero committed-data loss, repointed node3 to stream from node2, and rebuilt node1 as a standby of the new primary node2 via pg_basebackup (pg_rewind was unusable since data_checksums/wal_log_hints were off). Final topology: node2 = writable primary, node1 and node3 = standbys, matching the required "recovered former primary rejoins as standby of current primary" behavior. Then ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes (standbys first, primary last): captured boot_id + service health baseline, issued systemctl reboot with backgrounded ack, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed on every node, and verified PostgreSQL/replication/data fully recovered after each restart, ending with full 3-node cluster health and quorum.
